info.title: RunLab research API
info.summary: Pre-register a comparison, record per-seed results, get a verdict you can quote.
info.description:
Did my change actually help? Record each seed's metric for two arms (the change and its
baseline), then ask for a verdict: a paired test across seeds with its 95 % confidence
interval, checked against the plan you registered before the seeds ran.

**Auth.** Every call needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, your API token. An `agent`
token (the usual one for researchers and their coding agents) may call every operation here.

**Requests.** Bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`, at most 64 KiB). Every
response carries `X-Request-Id` (yours, if you sent one); quote it when you report a
problem. Errors are `{"error": "<what is wrong>"}` with status 400 (bad input), 401 (no or
bad token), 403 (role too low), 404 (no such id) or 413 (body too large).

**Stability.** `/api/v1` changes only by adding fields and operations.

Python client, guide and examples: https://github.com/omer-nachman/runlab-python

get.description:
The user name and role of the token. A cheap first call to check the URL and token.

Role: viewer or above.

role.description: Your access level: `agent` can call every operation here, `viewer` only reads.

post.description:
Records, before any seed runs, what you will compare and how: the arms, the primary
metric, the hypothesis, the most seeds per arm and the stopping rule. The plan is
hashed; `compareArms` later checks the comparison against it and reports deviations
(`prereg` in its response). Registering again for the same (project, a, b, metric)
needs `amend`, a reason, and keeps every version.

`power_check` estimates the power of `n_max` seeds from seeds already recorded for both
arms (a pilot); with none it is `unknown`.

Role: agent or above.

versions.description: How many times it was registered or amended.

power.description: Estimated power at n_max (with a pilot).

seeds_needed.description: Seeds per arm for min_power (with a pilot).

400.description: Bad input; `error` says what is wrong.

403.description: The token's role is below agent.

a.description: The treatment arm: the experiment name of your change.

n_max.description: Most seeds per arm you will run.

n_min.description: Fewest seeds per arm before a decision (default 2).

stopping.description: `msprt` (default: an always-valid sequential test; required by startStudy) or `fixed` (one compareArms call after all `n_max` seeds ran).

better.description: `higher`, `lower` or `auto` (default: lower for names with loss, error, err, perplexity, ppl, wer, cer, mse, mae, rmse, nll, latency, fid, regret; else higher).

amend.description: Why the plan changes; required to replace an existing plan.

post.description:
Stores `RESULT:` lines, one metric value of one arm on one seed per line:

    RESULT: <experiment> <metric>=<number> seed=<n> [<param>=<value> ...]

Names use letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-` (experiment names start with a letter).
Lines that do not start with `RESULT:` are ignored, so you can send a training log as
is. If any RESULT line is malformed nothing is stored (400). Sending the same line again
stores nothing (`already`), so retrying is safe.

Keep an arm's params identical across its seeds: different params make an arm several
configurations, and a comparison whose arms differ by more than 1.25x in configurations
is refused (`refused_by: equal_budget`).

Role: agent or above.

400.description: Bad input; `error` says what is wrong.

403.description: The token's role is below agent.

example.results:
RESULT: mixup acc=0.912 seed=0
RESULT: baseline acc=0.897 seed=0

post.summary: Compare two arms and record the verdict
post.description:
Tests arm `a` against arm `b` on `metric`. With at least 2 seeds both arms share it is a
paired t-test on the per-seed differences a − b (else Welch's t-test), with a 95 %
confidence interval. Before testing, checks run that can refuse the comparison
(verdict `refused`, `refused_by`, `why`), e.g. unequal tuning budgets.

Each call with new data is recorded as a look. Call it once, when the planned seeds have
run: a p-value read again and again as seeds come in no longer holds its alpha (the
response warns `peeking`). For valid early stopping, run a study.

An unknown project, arm or metric is a 400 that names the closest match.

Role: agent or above.

text.description: The verdict and its numbers in words.

diff.description: Mean of a − b over the seeds (positive: a scored higher).

p.description: Two-sided p-value; null with fewer than 2 seeds.

n.description: Seed pairs (paired) or the smaller arm's seeds.

looks.description: Distinct looks at this pair so far.

prereg.description: How the comparison matches the registered plan.

status.description: `ok`; `deviation` (see `issues`, e.g. analysed before `n_max` seeds, or the plan was registered after more than 3 seeds were seen); `missing` (no plan for this pair); `tampered` (the stored plan no longer matches its hash).

refused_by.description: The check that refused (only when refused).

example.text:
mixup vs baseline on acc (higher is better): mixup is better
  paired_t: diff +0.0178 [95% CI +0.0094, +0.0262], p=0.00098, n=10 (A 10, B 10)

400.description: Bad input; `error` says what is wrong.

403.description: The token's role is below agent.

better.description: `higher`, `lower` or `auto` (default, from the metric name; see registerPlan).

margin.description: Smallest difference that matters, in the metric's units. With it, a non-significant result can be `equivalent` or `non_inferior`.

get.description:
Recorded verdicts, newest first. A verdict is `stale` when data or a run under it was
marked bad since. With `recheck=1` the latest verdict of each pair is also judged again
on today's results (not counted as a look), in `recheck`.

Role: viewer or above.

parameters.name: recheck
parameters.description: `1` to judge each pair again on today's results.

stale.description: How many listed verdicts are stale; null when unknown.

inputs_changed.description: Same call on different RESULTs (seeds added or dropped).

stale.description: Absent when RunLab could not tell.

400.description: Bad input; `error` says what is wrong.

get.description:
Everything behind one recorded verdict: each seed's value per arm, the difference
re-derived from those values (`check`), and the verdict judged again on today's
results (`now.status`: `unchanged`, `inputs_changed` or `flipped`).

Role: viewer or above.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The verdict id, from listVerdicts or getResearchReport.

words.description: The verdict in a few words.

status.description: `unknown`: it could not be judged again.

400.description: Bad input; `error` says what is wrong.

get.description:
For each (a, b, metric) pair of a project, its latest verdict and whether a write-up
may quote it: `quotable`, `quotable_with_caveat` (tentative, e.g. fewer than 5 seeds per
arm) or `not_quotable`, with why and what to do next. A win must survive the
Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate `q` across every pair of the project (`m`
counts them all, whatever the filter). Each claim carries a ready-made `quote`.

Role: viewer or above.

parameters.name: arm
parameters.description: Only claims about this arm (either side).

m.description: Pairs counted for the FDR correction.

quote.description: The sentence to quote: a − b, 95 % CI, test, p, n.

400.description: Bad input; `error` says what is wrong.

post.summary: Let RunLab run a planned comparison's seeds
post.description:
RunLab runs seeds of both arms, one pair at a time, with the plan's sequential test
(register the plan with `stopping: msprt` first), and stops as soon as the evidence
decides, at `n_max`, or at `max_usd`, whichever comes first. It never spends more than
`max_usd`.

`command` names the training command to run. Every check runs before anything starts:
a refusal is a 400 whose `error` says why (unknown command, no msprt plan, cap too
high, too many running) and nothing is spent.

With `worker: true` the seeds run on your own machine instead: no `command`; give
`usd_per_hour`, what an hour of that machine costs. `runlab worker` (or
`RunLab.run_worker`) then asks workOnStudy for seed pairs, runs your training command
for both arms and posts the numbers until the study ends; each pair's reported run
time is charged against `max_usd`.

Role: agent or above.

400.description: Bad input; `error` says what is wrong.

403.description: The token's role is below agent.

command.description: One of your training command names; required unless `worker` is true.

params.description: Values for the command's placeholders, for both arms, e.g. `{"epochs": "10"}`. Letters, digits and `_.:+=-` only.

arm_params.description: Per-arm values, keyed by arm name, e.g. `{"mixup": {"alpha": "0.2"}}`.

worker.description: True: the seeds run on your machine (workOnStudy); default false.

usd_per_hour.description: With `worker`: what an hour of your machine costs, in dollars; each pair's run time is charged at it.

get.description:
Studies, newest first.

Role: viewer or above.

400.description: Bad input; `error` says what is wrong.

post.summary: Get the next seed pair of a worker study, and post the last one
post.description:
For a study started with `worker: true`. Post a finished pair (`seed`, its RESULT
lines in `results`, the arms that `failed`, its run time `wall_s`) and get the next
pair to run: its `seed`, the `arms` in run order (they alternate per seed) and the
`params` of each arm. `pair` is null with `retry_after_s` while other workers hold
every open pair, and null once the study ended (its `state` says how). Without `seed`
the call only asks. A pair stays reserved for its `worker` for `lease_s` seconds
(default 3600): ask again under the same name to get it back after a restart.

The plan's sequential test decides after each pair, exactly as for hosted studies; a
study stops at `n_max` pairs and before the next pair would pass `max_usd` at the
mean reported run time. A pair posted twice counts once. Bad input (another seed's or
another arm's lines, a seed outside the plan) is a 400 and stores nothing.

Role: agent or above.

arms.description: Both arms, in the order to run them.

params.description: Placeholder values per arm, keyed by arm name.

retry_after_s.description: With a null `pair` while running: ask again after this many seconds.

400.description: Bad input; `error` says what is wrong.

403.description: The token's role is below agent.

worker.description: This worker's name (letters, digits, `_.:-`); one name per machine or process.

seed.description: The finished pair's seed; omit to only ask for a pair.

results.description: The pair's RESULT lines (resultLine), one per line, with this `seed`.

failed.description: Arms whose run failed or printed no value; the pair then counts as failed.

wall_s.description: Seconds the pair took to run, both arms; charged at `usd_per_hour`.

lease_s.description: Seconds the next pair stays reserved for this worker (at most 7 days).

example.results:
RESULT experiment=mixup seed=0 acc=0.85
RESULT experiment=baseline seed=0 acc=0.80

get.description:
One study by id; poll it until `state` is no longer `running`.

Role: viewer or above.

400.description: Bad input; `error` says what is wrong.

message.description: What it means for this verdict and what to do.

CI.description: 95 % confidence interval of `diff`, [low, high]; null bounds when not computable.

VerdictCode.description:
`a_better` / `b_better`: p < alpha and the difference favours that arm (direction from
`better`). `no_detectable_difference`: p >= alpha; not evidence that the arms are equal.
`equivalent`: the CI lies inside ±`margin`. `non_inferior`: arm a is worse than b by
less than `margin`. `insufficient`: fewer than 2 seeds in an arm, so no test. `refused`:
a check (`refused_by`) would make any verdict untrustworthy; `why` says what to fix.

mode.description: `worker`: its seeds run on your machine (workOnStudy, `runlab worker`); `hosted`: RunLab runs them.

command.description: The training command name it runs; empty when `mode` is `worker`.

usd_per_hour.description: The price it is charged at; for `worker`, what an hour of your machine costs.

n_max.description: Most seeds per arm (from the plan).

deadline_at.description: Unix seconds when the cap is reached at its price; null for `worker` (its cap counts reported run time).

decision.description: Once ended: `A` or `B` (that arm won), `futile` (no detectable difference at this budget), `equivalent`, `budget` or `continue` (undecided).

winner.description: The winning arm's name; null unless `decision` is `A` or `B`.

detail.description: Why it failed or was refused; empty otherwise.
